title: Israel election: what the exit polls show
lines: Israel has voted, and the exit polls point to a deadlock.
These are exit polls from Israel's three main TV channels, not official results.
Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud is projected as the largest party, with twenty-four to twenty-five seats.
Former army chief Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party is close behind, with twenty-one to twenty-three.
Naftali Bennett's party is projected at twelve to fourteen seats.
But Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc is projected at only about fifty seats. The opposition bloc is at fifty-two to fifty-three. A government needs sixty-one.
Arab parties are projected at seventeen to eighteen seats, which could make them decisive.
Turnout was the highest in decades. Ynet reports seventy-four point three percent had voted by eight in the evening.
Netanyahu claimed the right had won a decisive majority among Zionist voters, and said he plans to form a right-wing government. Eisenkot had urged him to accept defeat and step down.
More than six hundred and fifty thousand special ballots, including soldiers' votes, are counted separately, and could still shift a few seats.
Official results are due by the fourth of November. Then the president asks a leader to try to build a coalition, which could take weeks.
